c: These experiences need different descriptions and assessment; they are not all established ADHD manifestations.
Not a sequence. Not all established ADHD manifestations.
Losing an intention: the plan drops before the action.
Losing track of time: clock time passes; the activity may still be remembered.
Automatic familiar activity: a practised action with little attention; often reconstructable afterwards.
Actual gap in awareness: a period that cannot be accounted for. Needs its own assessment.

c: The prefrontal cortex holds goals online and screens out distraction; its function depends on finely tuned dopamine and noradrenaline signalling.

Pain and physical effort may consume the same limited control capacity, so cognitive slips worsen on bad physical days. This is a plausible link to test in your own records, not an established finding.
